subject: Pilot economics + tech guardrails for inference savings (FinServe AI)
messages:
From: Emma Chen <emma@finserve.ai>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@finserve.ai
Date: 2027-07-29T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot ask — structure & technical constraints

Connor — great talking this morning. We want to run a 6-week pilot to validate latency and token cost improvements for our customer-facing assistants. Two asks from our side: (1) a simple pricing structure for the pilot (credits, per-token, or commit) so procurement can approve quickly; (2) clear technical guardrails: which quantization levels you recommend, expected accuracy delta, and batching/cache implications for our 512-token median requests.

Can you send a one-page economics proposal and the technical tradeoffs? Procurement would like any legal/DocuSign-ready pilot agreement in parallel.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Chen
Head of ML Products, FinServe AI
emma@finserve.ai
From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: Emma Chen <emma@finserve.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-07-30T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask — structure & technical constraints

Emma — thanks, summarized below and attached a short PDF + appendix. High-level pilot proposal (attached: FS-2384_pilot_econ_v1.pdf):

- Duration: 6 weeks (production-slice)
- Commit: $30k pilot credit + up to $10k usage overage (billed monthly) — we can convert credits to startup discount on early conversion.
- SKU breakdown: hosted inference per-token baseline for unquantized model + pilot credit applied first.
- Operational concession: 1 day of integration support + weekly syncs with Connor (me) and Aditya.

Technical guardrails (short form):
- Quantization: recommend starting with 8-bit PTQ for the Llama-variant we discussed. Expected median accuracy delta: ~0.5–1.5% on our internal classification evals; see appendix for dataset breakdown. 4-bit QAT is possible but increases engineering cycles and can introduce 2–4% delta on edge cases.
- Batching: for median 512-token requests, continuous batching at a 30–60ms scheduling window yields ~1.6x throughput improvement with <10ms P95 latency increase. We can tune the window per route.
- KV/prefix cache: enable prefix caching for repeated system prompts — expected 15–25% token savings for conversational flows. Requires lightweight client header to indicate session affinity.
- Fallbacks: we recommend an unquantized fallback model for high-confidence scoring slices (fraud/risk flows). Redwood can route by policy.

I'll loop Aditya for pricing flexibility and Laura for the pilot contract. Attaching a DocuSign stub for procurement to review.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Emma Chen <emma@finserve.ai>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@finserve.ai
Date: 2027-08-01T14:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask — structure & technical constraints

Connor — this is helpful. A couple follow-ups from procurement and ML:

1) Procurement: can you (a) make the pilot credit refundable if we fail to meet scheduled milestones, or (b) convert unused credits to platform credit for our pilot customers? We want a simple path to return unspent funds.
2) ML team: curious about how quantization interacts with our existing reranker. Has Redwood validated 8-bit on retrieval-augmented scoring? Any recommended eval prompts we should run to measure hallucination risk?

Also, curious if you can provide a short runbook for the batching window adjustments — our SRE wants to understand how to change the scheduler without impacting P95.

If those answers look okay we'll push to procurement for a signature.

—Emma
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Emma Chen <emma@finserve.ai>
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-03T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask — structure & technical constraints

Emma — quick answers and concessions to keep procurement moving: (a) refundable credit: we can offer a milestone-based refund policy for the pilot (up to 50% refundable if SLAs not met and failure attributable to Redwood). We'll detail this in the DocuSign stub. (b) Unused credits can be converted to platform credit valid for 12 months if you convert to a paid contract within 90 days — otherwise credits expire.

Technical follow-ups (from our infra/ML):
- 8-bit PTQ + Reranker: we've validated 8-bit PTQ across multiple retrieval-backed scoring flows. In our internal evals the top-k reranker rank stability remains >97% compared to FP16 on standard IR datasets; hallucination risk increase measured <1% in classification/regression slices but can surface in long-context generative responses. We recommend running your critical eval prompts (we attached a sample eval sheet in the appendix) focusing on retrieval-anchored queries.
- Eval prompts: use a mix of (a) exact-match retrieval checks, (b) factually-grounded Q&A, and (c) open-ended generative prompts that include retrieved documents. We'll provide a template and can run a batch eval on a 1000-sample slice as part of the pilot.
- Batching runbook: see quant-batch-recommendation-appendix.xlsx for prescriptive scheduler knobs. TL;DR: start with a 40ms window with a max batch size cap, monitor token-per-second and P95 — lowering window reduces latency but increases cost. We'll include SRE runbook steps in the shared Drive doc if you want.

Next steps: (1) I'll update the PDF to include the refundable-credit language and send a DocuSign link; (2) Connor & Laura will schedule the kickoff and the joint eval plan.

Thanks — Aditya Rao
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
